=================== github/workflows/deploy-prod.yml
     1	# Reusable production deploy (framework layer 3 "Merge approval = deploy approval", layer 5).
     2	# The ONLY workflow that references the `production` environment. Called by deploy-on-main.yml.
     3	#
     4	# Conditions this file must keep (checked by examples/tests/test_workflow_policy.py):
     5	# - no ref/SHA input: it deploys the commit that was merged (github.sha of the push to main);
     6	# - one concurrency group per stack without cancel-in-progress, so a running deploy is never
     7	#   cancelled (Pulumi guide: that can leave infrastructure half-applied). GitHub still cancels
     8	#   a run that is only *pending* when a newer one arrives, so not every merged commit gets its
     9	#   own deploy run; the newer run deploys both commits;
    10	# - OIDC only (id-token: write); no AWS keys; every action pinned to a full commit SHA;
    11	# - it deploys only the current tip of main: re-running an old run (allowed for writers for 30
    12	#   days, same GITHUB_SHA) would otherwise roll prod back without any approval;
    13	# - prod preview -> risk stop -> apply; the risk stop step cannot be skipped or ignored.
    14	#   No --skip-preview/-f, --target/-t, --exclude, --replace, state, import, destroy.
    15	#
    16	# Known limits (examples/README.md): the stack's own code (the Pulumi program, Serverless
    17	# plugins) runs with the deploy role during preview and apply, so the risk stop
    18	# catches risky diffs nobody looked at, not malicious code that was approved. `pulumi up`
    19	# previews again; a change made outside the pipeline between the two previews is not re-checked.
    20	#
    21	# Variables of the `production` environment (not secrets): AWS_REGION,
    22	# PROD_PULUMI_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, PROD_SERVERLESS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN, PULUMI_BACKEND_URL,
    23	# PULUMI_CLI_VERSION, NODE_VERSION. The Serverless License Key is read from
    24	# SSM Parameter Store with the deploy role (sf >= 4.4.19, R4.4.8), so no CI secret holds it.
    25	name: deploy-prod
    26	
    27	on:
    28	  workflow_call:
    29	    inputs:
    30	      stack:
    31	        description: Stack name, e.g. claims-data. Also the deploy-approvals/<stack>/ directory.
    32	        type: string
    33	        required: true
    34	      tool:
    35	        description: "pulumi or serverless"
    36	        type: string
    37	        required: true
    38	      workdir:
    39	        description: Directory of the stack in the monorepo
    40	        type: string
    41	        required: true
    42	
    43	permissions: {}
    44	
    45	jobs:
    46	  deploy:
    47	    name: deploy ${{ inputs.stack }} to production
    48	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    49	    environment: production
    50	    permissions:
    51	      contents: read   # check out the merged commit
    52	      id-token: write  # OIDC to the prod deploy role; no stored AWS keys
    53	    concurrency:
    54	      group: deploy-prod-${{ inputs.stack }}
    55	      cancel-in-progress: false
    56	    env:
    57	      STACK: ${{ inputs.stack }}
    58	      TOOL: ${{ inputs.tool }}
    59	      WORKDIR: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
    60	    steps:
    61	      - name: Check out the merged commit, with history for the risk-stop approval checks
    62	        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
    63	        with:
    64	          persist-credentials: false
    65	          fetch-depth: 0
    66	
    67	      - name: Set up Node.js
    68	        uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
    69	        with:
    70	          node-version: ${{ vars.NODE_VERSION }}
    71	
    72	      - name: Refuse to deploy anything but the current tip of main
    73	        env:
    74	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    75	          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
    76	        run: |
    77	          # git/ref/heads/main names the branch explicitly; a tag called `main` cannot match.
    78	          tip=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/git/ref/heads/main" --jq .object.sha)
    79	          if [ "$tip" != "$GITHUB_SHA" ]; then
    80	            echo "This run is for $GITHUB_SHA but main is at $tip (re-run, or a newer merge)."
    81	            echo "Nothing is deployed; the run for the newer commit deploys both."
    82	            echo "If no newer run exists (e.g. its message had [skip ci]), merge an empty change."
    83	            exit 1
    84	          fi
    85	
    86	      # Everything that downloads code is installed here, before the AWS credentials are in the
    87	      # job's environment. Install scripts can still request the job's OIDC token (id-token:
    88	      # write is job-wide) or leave a process behind (examples/README.md, "Limits").
    89	      - name: Install dependencies before any prod credential exists in the job
    90	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
    91	        run: npm ci
    92	
    93	      - name: Install the Pulumi CLI only
    94	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
    95	        uses: pulumi/actions@8e5e406f4007fca908480587cb9893c07090f58d # v7.0.0
    96	        with:
    97	          pulumi-version: ${{ vars.PULUMI_CLI_VERSION }}
    98	
    99	      - name: Install Pulumi plugins and the policy pack before credentials
   100	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   101	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   102	        run: |
   103	          pulumi install
   104	          cd "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/policy-packs/aws"
   105	          npm ci
   106	          pulumi install
   107	
   108	      # ⚠️ From memory, not verified: Serverless v4's npm package downloads the framework on
   109	      # first run. Running it once here keeps that download before the credentials. Whether
   110	      # `--version` works before authentication (R4.4.8) is also unverified.
   111	      - name: Install the Serverless Framework before credentials
   112	        if: inputs.tool == 'serverless'
   113	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}
   114	        run: npx serverless --version
   115	
   116	      # Two roles (framework layer 1; SCP in examples/aws/scp-prod-ou.json): only the Pulumi role is
   117	      # exempt from the Lambda-update deny; the Serverless role only passes the CloudFormation
   118	      # deploymentRole. This stops drift from `serverless deploy function`; it does NOT stop
   119	      # malicious code in this job, which can request its own OIDC token for either role
   120	      # (examples/README.md, "Limits"). One step per tool, so an unset variable fails the step
   121	      # instead of falling back to the other role.
   122	      - name: AWS credentials through GitHub OIDC (Pulumi deploy role)
   123	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   124	        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@e1253824e5c10ff9df46874f81ed3ec929e19cfd # v6.3.0
   125	        with:
   126	          role-to-assume: ${{ vars.PROD_PULUMI_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN }}

    16	  codeowners-validate:

    18	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04

     8	#   a run that is only *pending* when a newer one arrives, so not every merged commit gets its

   129	          role-session-name: deploy-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}

   136	          aws-region: ${{ vars.AWS_REGION }}

   139	      - name: Preview prod (Pulumi)
   140	        if: inputs.tool == 'pulumi'
   141	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}

   149	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}

   154	      # Risk stop (layer 3). Exit 0: no risky change, or a valid approval matches this preview.

   156	      # exit fails the job here, before any Apply step. The summary goes to the job summary and
   157	      # lists resource type, name, operation and changed property names, never values.

   161	          --tool "$TOOL" --preview "$RUNNER_TEMP/preview.json"

   174	      # policy violation stops the update (R4.2.2). This is the phase-2 shape: until the policy

   176	      - name: Apply (Pulumi)

   178	        working-directory: ${{ inputs.workdir }}

     1	# Required check `codeowners-validate` (ruleset-main.json; framework layer 5).
     2	# GitHub silently skips invalid CODEOWNERS lines and owners that do not exist or lack write
     3	# access, so a typo can remove an approval requirement without anyone noticing. This job fails
     4	# the PR when GitHub reports any CODEOWNERS error for the PR's head commit.
     5	# Note: GitHub applies the CODEOWNERS file of the BASE branch to a PR; this check stops a broken
     6	# file from reaching main in the first place.
     7	name: codeowners-validate
     8	
     9	on:
    10	  pull_request:
    11	    branches: [main]
    12	
    13	permissions: {}
    14	
    15	jobs:
    16	  codeowners-validate:
    17	    name: codeowners-validate
    18	    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    19	    permissions:
    20	      contents: read  # read CODEOWNERS errors for this repository
    21	    concurrency:
    22	      group: codeowners-validate-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
    23	      cancel-in-progress: true
    24	    steps:
    25	      - name: Ask GitHub for CODEOWNERS errors
    26	        env:
    27	          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
    28	          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
    29	          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
    30	        run: |
    31	          errors=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/codeowners/errors?ref=$HEAD_SHA" --jq '.errors | length')
    32	          if [ "$errors" != "0" ]; then
    33	            gh api "repos/$REPO/codeowners/errors?ref=$HEAD_SHA" \
    34	              --jq '.errors[] | "line \(.line): \(.kind) \(.message)"'
    35	            exit 1
    36	          fi
    37	          echo "CODEOWNERS: no errors"

=================== claude/marketplace/plugins/devsecops-guardrails/skills/prod-change/SKILL.md
     1	---
     2	name: prod-change
     3	description: Use when the user wants to change anything in production. Explains the only allowed path - a pull request applied by CI - and what to do in an incident.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Changing production
     7	
     8	1. Never change production from this session. Production is written only by the deploy
     9	   workflow after a reviewed pull request is merged to `main` (framework layer 3).
    10	2. Prepare the change as code (Pulumi, `serverless.yml`, Kubernetes manifests), preview it
    11	   against non-prod, and ask the engineer to push the branch and open the pull request: under
    12	   the managed sandbox this session has no git or GitHub credentials. A code owner who is not
    13	   the engineer approves it; an agent never approves a pull request (OD5).
    14	3. If the deploy stops at the risk stop, open a pull request that adds only
    15	   `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<stopped commit>.yaml` with the hash from the job summary.
    16	4. In an incident: label the pull request `incident`; the on-call approver reviews it.
    17	   If the pull request path cannot be used at all, the incident responder requests a JIT grant
    18	   with a command list; that terminal runs no agent (framework layer 7).

=================== risk-stop/deploy-approvals/claims-data/0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567.yaml
     1	# Risk-stop approval (framework layer 3, ADR-0004). File name = the stopped commit.
     2	# Opened as a PR by the original author; approved by an owner of the stack (CODEOWNERS on
     3	# deploy-approvals/claims-data/), usually the first PR's approver, who now sees the prod diff.
     4	# The approver's identity is the PR review in GitHub, not anything written in this file.
     5	# classify.py accepts it only if: stopped_commit is a strict ancestor of HEAD; this file was
     6	# added after it, by a commit that changes nothing outside deploy-approvals/claims-data/; and
     7	# that commit is at most 7 days older than HEAD. The values below are placeholders.

=================== claude/marketplace/plugins/devsecops-guardrails/skills/prod-change/SKILL.md
     1	---
     2	name: prod-change
     3	description: Use when the user wants to change anything in production. Explains the only allowed path - a pull request applied by CI - and what to do in an incident.
     4	---
     5	
     6	# Changing production
     7	
     8	1. Never change production from this session. Production is written only by the deploy
     9	   workflow after a reviewed pull request is merged to `main` (framework layer 3).
    10	2. Prepare the change as code (Pulumi, `serverless.yml`, Kubernetes manifests), preview it
    11	   against non-prod, and ask the engineer to push the branch and open the pull request: under
    12	   the managed sandbox this session has no git or GitHub credentials. A code owner who is not
    13	   the engineer approves it; an agent never approves a pull request (OD5).
    14	3. If the deploy stops at the risk stop, open a pull request that adds only
    15	   `deploy-approvals/<stack>/<stopped commit>.yaml` with the hash from the job summary.
    16	4. In an incident: label the pull request `incident`; the on-call approver reviews it.
    17	   If the pull request path cannot be used at all, the incident responder requests a JIT grant
    18	   with a command list; that terminal runs no agent (framework layer 7).

5. **Classification beyond the framework's categories** [design]: the property-name rule, the
   audit/detection category and "an unknown operation stops" go beyond layer 3's list
   (stateful replace/delete, IAM, network, policy finding).
6. **The approval hash must cover changed values**, not only resource names, or an approval for
   one IAM policy would let a different change to the same policy through; and it must leave out
   values that change on every build, or an approval never matches. ⚠️ From memory, not checked:
   Serverless puts a timestamped path in the Lambda `Code.S3Key` and a code hash in
   `AWS::Lambda::Version` logical IDs; both are left out of the hash.
7. **Fail-safe CODEOWNERS default** [design]: without it, root `package.json`, a new stack or a new
   `deploy-approvals/<stack>/` folder would be unowned, and GitHub then accepts an approval from
   any writer (📖 about code owners).
8. **Same-repository reusable workflows can use `uses: $/.github/workflows/<file>`**, which GitHub
   now recommends: it resolves to the running commit, not to the runner's workspace (📖 GitHub docs
   source, `data/reusables/actions/reusable-workflow-calling-syntax.md`; flagged by zizmor's
   `self-repository` audit). `actionlint` 1.7.12 (✅ latest release on 2026-11-09, published
   2026-03-30) does not know the syntax; `validate.sh` ignores only that message.
9. **`runner.temp` is not available in job-level `env`** (✅ caught by `actionlint`); paths use
   `$RUNNER_TEMP` inside steps.

### Step 2 (identity and access)

10. **SCP "protect the org trail" is mostly redundant** for member accounts: they cannot delete
    an organization trail or turn its logging off anyway (📖 R2.6.2). E5 instead denies changes
    to any trail inside prod accounts. The framework's layer-1 bullet is reworded in the final pass.
11. **"Metadata" reads can leak configuration, data or secrets** (⚠️ response contents from
    memory of the API references): `lambda:ListFunctions` and `ecs:DescribeTaskDefinition` return
    environment variables and cannot be limited to one resource (✅ catalogue: not resource-scoped);
    `lambda:GetFunction` also returns a code download URL; `ecs:DescribeTasks` returns container
    environment overrides; `cloudformation:DescribeStacks` returns stack outputs (it could be scoped
    per stack); `cloudformation:DescribeStackEvents` returns `ResourceProperties`, "the properties
    used to create the resource" (📖 [StackEvent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/APIReference/API_StackEvent.html)),
    which for a function includes its environment variables (⚠️ inferred); `logs:DescribeQueries`
    returns other users' query strings. E6 leaves all of them out [design];
    `lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration` is granted per function instead.
12. **AWS's annotations are signals, not a classification of customer data**: `IsDataPlane` marks
    `cloudwatch:GetMetricData` too; `sqs:ListQueues` is not marked `IsList`; and many `IsList`
    actions return data or configuration (`s3:ListBucket` object keys, `ec2:Describe*` launch
    templates, `ssm:ListCommandInvocations` output; ✅ annotations in the catalogue, ⚠️ response
    contents from memory). The tests use an explicit allowlist for `Resource: "*"`. One entry has a
    condition: `states:ListExecutions` returns execution names, so names must not be built from
    claim data [design].
13. **Two prod deploy roles** (framework layer 1 already implies it): the SCP exempts the Pulumi
    role from the Lambda-update deny, but not the Serverless role, so `serverless deploy function`
    cannot change a function outside CloudFormation (drift). It does not stop malicious code in
    the job (Limits). `deploy-prod.yml` has one credentials step per tool, so an unset role
    variable fails instead of falling back to the other role.
14. **The claim-data deny assumes a naming convention** [design]: every legitimate reader must
    match `app-claims-*` or a `DataRead-*` permission set. Lambda execution roles behind SQS event
    sources, Step Functions execution roles and an AWS Backup role that reads the bucket would be
    denied otherwise (only service-linked roles are outside SCPs, 📖 R2.3.2). Phase-2 prerequisite:
    inventory the real callers of these actions (CloudTrail, IAM last-accessed data) and add them
    before the SCP is attached.
15. **The trail deny blocks every principal in prod accounts**, including deploy roles and
    `OrganizationAccountAccessRole`: a member-account trail can only be changed after a temporary
    change to the SCP (an L3 path), or an exempt audit role would have to be added [design].
16. **Exempt role names must be protected** (OD19): the exemptions are name patterns, so anyone in
    a prod account who could create or re-trust a role named `app-claims-*` or `cfn-deployment-*`
    would bypass both denies. E5 lets only `github-prod-deploy-pulumi` change those roles.
    - **Today that role deploys every Pulumi stack**, not only the IAM stack, and any job in the
      deploy workflow can obtain it (OD20). So "only the IAM stack" holds only after OD20 gives the
      IAM stack its own role and OIDC subject; until then the protection is "only an approved prod
      Pulumi deploy" (agent's reading of OD19, confirmed by the owner 2026-11-09).
    - **Residual risks:** a principal that may pass an `app-claims-*` role could create a new
      function with it (`lambda:CreateFunction` is not denied), and one that may pass
      `cfn-deployment-*` to CloudFormation could change any function through a template;
      `iam:PassRole` is left out on purpose because the Serverless role must pass
      `cfn-deployment-*`. An `InfraOperator-*` grant may change an `app-claims` function's code
      and so read claim data indirectly (accepted with break-glass, ADR-0005; JIT reconciliation
      in layer 7 is the control).
    - **Constraints and prerequisites (phase 2):** Serverless services cannot create their own
      `app-claims-*` execution roles (CloudFormation runs as `cfn-deployment-*`, not exempt); those
      roles live in the Pulumi IAM stack and are referenced by ARN. The protected roles must exist
      before the SCP is attached, and if `github-prod-deploy-pulumi`'s own trust breaks (e.g. the
      subject-format opt-in of E4), only an SCP change from the management account (an L3 path)
      can repair it.
17. **Gaps in the claim-data deny, under G13** (⚠️ not verified): S3 requests through access

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.
