questions.question: #1 (major): bản "minimum safe phase 1" trong rollout hoãn 1.4 (chuyển deploy từ laptop sang CI) và 1.8 (các check S10), nhưng phase 1 vẫn gỡ quyền ghi prod và ruleset phase 1 vẫn bắt buộc các check đó. Sửa thế nào?

options.label: Thêm vào prerequisite (Recommended)
options.description: Đưa 1.4 và một bản 1.1 tối thiểu (đo incident lane) vào hard prerequisites; ruleset phase 1 chỉ bắt các check đã có, còn lại thêm vào ở phase 2; chỉnh S9–S11 và C-09/C-15/C-17 cho khớp. Thêm khoảng 5–8 pd vào phase 1.

options.label: Lùi việc gỡ quyền ghi
options.description: Giữ nguyên bản minimum, nhưng việc gỡ quyền ghi prod thường trực (1.16) lùi sang đầu phase 2, sau khi 1.4 và 1.8 xong. Phase 1 nhẹ hơn, nhưng quyền ghi thường trực tồn tại lâu hơn.

questions.question: #2 (major): SCP chỉ miễn trừ role deploy của IAM stack, nên "đêm sửa IAM stack thì dùng JIT" không thực hiện được (JIT bị SCP chặn). Chọn đường cho đêm?

options.label: Rule incident trên PR (Recommended)
options.description: Ban đêm, PR vào IAM stack được duyệt bởi on-call approver và một L3 owner gọi qua điện thoại (gate app đếm 2 người); vẫn đi đường PR, không cần sửa SCP.

options.label: Miễn trừ InfraOperator-iam
options.description: Thêm một permission set JIT riêng cho IAM được SCP miễn trừ, với rule duyệt riêng (2 người). Có đường JIT nhưng mở rộng tập role miễn trừ.

options.label: Ghi rõ: không có đường đêm
options.description: Chấp nhận rủi ro: thay đổi IAM stack chờ đến giờ làm việc; ghi vào giới hạn §1a.

questions.question: #3 (major): MDM là điều kiện then chốt (thiếu MDM thì đổi login/API key là bỏ qua được managed settings; S5 gần như không đạt) nhưng không nằm trong danh sách quyết định của Papaya. Xử lý?

options.label: Thêm vào quyết định (Recommended)
options.description: Thêm "MDM trên laptop engineer" vào bảng Decisions Papaya must take, có khuyến nghị (có MDM trước phase 2) và nói rõ hệ quả nếu không; S5 ghi là chỉ đạt khi có MDM.

options.label: Chỉ sửa S5
options.description: Không thêm quyết định; ghi lại S5 là mục tiêu không đạt khi thiếu MDM.

questions.question: Các finding còn lại: chọn những mục muốn làm (bỏ trống = giữ nguyên, ghi lại lý do).

options.label: #5 Chi phí vận hành
options.description: Ước tính công sức vận hành hằng năm của tooling tự xây, và đưa "degraded mode" (rule GitHub có sẵn + check E12 hằng đêm) thành lựa chọn v1 rõ ràng. Lưu ý: phần định cỡ rota lần trước bạn đã chọn không làm (#10).

options.label: #6 Runtime riêng cho agent
options.description: Đánh giá một runtime tách biệt (devcontainer/máy từ xa, không có SSO cache của người, role riêng) như một lựa chọn phase 2 có chi phí; nói rõ P-row nào chuyển sang Covered.

options.label: #4 Viết lại thành văn xuôi
options.description: Viết lại các layer theo trạng thái hiện tại, bỏ chuỗi mã OD/Options/framing trong thân bài (chuyển vào chú thích hoặc phụ lục). Việc lớn, rủi ro làm lệch nội dung.

options.label: #9 Định nghĩa data owner
options.description: Data owner = nhân viên Papaya được chỉ định cho từng tenant (không phải người của insurer); nêu quyền truy cập và vì sao.

options.description: Giữ nguyên bản minimum, nhưng việc gỡ quyền ghi prod thường trực (1.16) lùi sang đầu phase 2, sau khi 1.4 và 1.8 xong. Phase 1 nhẹ hơn, nhưng quyền ghi thường trực tồn tại lâu hơn.

questions.question: #2 (major): SCP chỉ miễn trừ role deploy của IAM stack, nên "đêm sửa IAM stack thì dùng JIT" không thực hiện được (JIT bị SCP chặn). Chọn đường cho đêm?

options.label: Rule incident trên PR (Recommended)
options.description: Ban đêm, PR vào IAM stack được duyệt bởi on-call approver và một L3 owner gọi qua điện thoại (gate app đếm 2 người); vẫn đi đường PR, không cần sửa SCP.

options.label: Miễn trừ InfraOperator-iam
options.description: Thêm một permission set JIT riêng cho IAM được SCP miễn trừ, với rule duyệt riêng (2 người). Có đường JIT nhưng mở rộng tập role miễn trừ.

options.label: Ghi rõ: không có đường đêm
options.description: Chấp nhận rủi ro: thay đổi IAM stack chờ đến giờ làm việc; ghi vào giới hạn §1a.

questions.question: #3 (major): MDM là điều kiện then chốt (thiếu MDM thì đổi login/API key là bỏ qua được managed settings; S5 gần như không đạt) nhưng không nằm trong danh sách quyết định của Papaya. Xử lý?

options.label: Thêm vào quyết định (Recommended)
options.description: Thêm "MDM trên laptop engineer" vào bảng Decisions Papaya must take, có khuyến nghị (có MDM trước phase 2) và nói rõ hệ quả nếu không; S5 ghi là chỉ đạt khi có MDM.

options.label: Chỉ sửa S5
options.description: Không thêm quyết định; ghi lại S5 là mục tiêu không đạt khi thiếu MDM.

questions.question: Các finding còn lại: chọn những mục muốn làm (bỏ trống = giữ nguyên, ghi lại lý do).

options.label: #5 Chi phí vận hành
options.description: Ước tính công sức vận hành hằng năm của tooling tự xây, và đưa "degraded mode" (rule GitHub có sẵn + check E12 hằng đêm) thành lựa chọn v1 rõ ràng. Lưu ý: phần định cỡ rota lần trước bạn đã chọn không làm (#10).

options.label: #6 Runtime riêng cho agent
options.description: Đánh giá một runtime tách biệt (devcontainer/máy từ xa, không có SSO cache của người, role riêng) như một lựa chọn phase 2 có chi phí; nói rõ P-row nào chuyển sang Covered.

options.label: #4 Viết lại thành văn xuôi
options.description: Viết lại các layer theo trạng thái hiện tại, bỏ chuỗi mã OD/Options/framing trong thân bài (chuyển vào chú thích hoặc phụ lục). Việc lớn, rủi ro làm lệch nội dung.

options.label: #9 Định nghĩa data owner
options.description: Data owner = nhân viên Papaya được chỉ định cho từng tenant (không phải người của insurer); nêu quyền truy cập và vì sao.

answers.Các finding còn lại: chọn những mục muốn: #5 Chi phí vận hành, #6 Runtime riêng cho agent, #4 Viết lại thành văn xuôi, #9 Định nghĩa data owner

# Rollout plan: 45 / 75 / 100 days

> Status: moved out of framework layer 8 on 2026-11-09 and expanded. The items, their order and the
> phase-1 subset were approved with the framework (OD4, OD7, OD21); the allowlist became two repo
> scripts after examples finding 19. Added here and approved by the author (owner of this submission, not Papaya) on
> 2026-11-09 ("done when" checks stay [design]): the owner and "done when" of each item, the "measured from" column, item 2.9 (from OD15,
> OD20), the run-log export in 2.4 (from layer 3, G7) and the S4 risk (framing §5). After the
> independent review, the owner approved fixes that add or change items (from OD22: 1.6, 1.12, 1.15, 1.17,
> 1.18, 1.19–1.23, 1.11, 2.2, 2.4, 2.9, 2.10; from OD31: 1.6, 1.8, 1.11, 1.13, 1.16, 2.8, 2.11–2.13,
> S4 and the effort estimate) · Updated:
> 2026-11-09 · Builds on [`01-framework.md`](01-framework.md)

## How to read this

The rollout takes about 100 days (re-baselined from the 90 of GĐ-12 after the effort estimate, OD49). Effort is estimated roughly in
[Load and risks](#load-and-risks) (⚠️ no Papaya data): the 23 phase-1 items do not fit 30 days with
1–2 people, so that section names the minimum safe phase 1 and the headcount it needs (OD35), and
phase 1 now runs 45 days; the items that do not fit move into the first weeks of phase 2. Markers and codes are those of the
[framework](01-framework.md#how-to-read-this). "Done when" is the check that closes an item
[design]; examples `E1`–`E19` (with E3b, E4b, E9b) are the expected configuration in [`examples/`](../examples/README.md).

**Owners** (framework layer 8): **DS** DevSecOps (1–2 people, GĐ-1) · **PL** a platform team or the
named engineers who own deploy workflows (whether Papaya has a platform team is unknown ⚠️) ·
**CO** Compliance · **EL** engineering leads · **EM** engineering management.

**Order.** Framing Q8 ranked the first 30 days: (1) remove long-lived CI credentials, (2) narrow
standing prod access, (3) the MCP/plugin catalogue; the on-call approver list comes before or with (2).
One rule from layer 8 shapes the whole plan: **access is never removed before its replacement works.**

## Phase 1 — days 0–45: the pull request becomes the default prod write path

| # | Item | Owner | Done when | Layer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | Measure the incident PR lane on one service. First task once that service has an OIDC deploy workflow (Options §9). Include the prompt for each `aws` read, which the allowlist does not cover | DS, PL | Decision-to-apply time measured; the target is ≤ 30 min | 3, 7 |
| 1.2 | Scan non-prod for real data | DS, CO | First scan result recorded (S11) | 6 |
| 1.3 | OIDC for deploy workflows; remove long-lived keys, except k0s/Firebase under OD1 | PL | No AWS access key used by a workflow (S2, with the OD1 caveat); E4 trust policy applied | 1, 5 |
| 1.4 | Move laptop deploys to CI (GĐ-10, unconfirmed) | PL | No laptop deploy in CloudTrail since the move | 1 |
| 1.5 | Rulesets, CODEOWNERS and the CODEOWNERS validation check | DS; EL decide CODEOWNERS content | E1, E2 and `codeowners-validate` live on `main`; a test PR shows whether "Update branch" keeps approvals (OD31) | 3, 5 |
| 1.6 | The approval-gate app (decision logic E12): human approvals only, kept across a branch update that leaves the diff unchanged (OD31), two L3 owner team members on process paths (OD26), on-call approvals for another team only with an open incident and on shift (OD27), flagged approvals in the monthly report. Live before or with 1.5, whose ruleset requires its check (G19). Rolled out in two steps (OD49): two weeks report-only, where the app posts its result but the ruleset does not yet require it and every failure it would have caused is reviewed; then required. Availability target: 99.5 % of working hours, and an alert when it has not answered a PR event within 5 minutes [design]; if it is down longer than an hour, the controlled removal of the required check (layer 3: two L3 approvals, alerted, time-boxed) is the tested fallback | DS | App is the required source of the `approval-gate` check; a test PR shows each rule; the report-only fortnight reviewed; the removal runbook drilled once | 3 |
| 1.7 | Remove human write kubeconfigs for prod k0s (interim) | PL | No human holds a prod k0s write kubeconfig | 1 |
| 1.8 | S10 checks (OD39): `dependency-check` (Dependabot plus a lockfile scanner), `secret-scan` and `sast` (GitHub Secret Protection and Code Security if Papaya buys them, else open-source scanners), `iac-scan` (Trivy), `workflow-lint`, `pr-size`. Access Analyzer and policy packs follow in phase 2, so until then OD8 relies on the risk stop alone | DS | Required checks on every PR to `main` (S10) | 5 |
| 1.9 | Minimal real-data read flow: request, 1-hour data-read role, approver ≠ requester, data-owner review afterwards | DS, CO | One request handled end to end | 6 |
| 1.10 | `ProdReadMetadata` becomes the only standing prod role. Existing broad read roles go only once 1.9 works | DS | E6 assigned; broad read roles removed | 1 |
| 1.11 | Start moving secrets to runtime resolution and redacting logs at source, service by service. A log group opens to `ProdReadMetadata` only after its masking policy is set (E14) and the SAST rule against logging whole events passes for that service (OD28) | PL, service owners | First services done, each with masking and the SAST rule; list of the rest with dates: every claims service by the end of phase 2 (day 75), the rest by day 100 (OD34; ⚠️ estimate) | 1, 6 |
| 1.12 | On-call approver schedule and a minimal incident-responder schedule, named, 24/7. On-call approvers only approve (OD7). The approver schedule is the file `oncall/schedule.yaml` (an L3 path) that the approval-gate app reads; incidents are Linear issues (OD27) | EM | Both schedules published with primary and backup (S7); the app reads the file | 3, 7 |
| 1.13 | Minimal JIT fallback: the Linear request template (scope as a `jit-scope` label, the incident as an issue relation) and a receiver that grants only after its pre-grant check, once per request, with the scoped role of E16 (OD33, OD41); before building it, a real webhook payload is captured and the AWS TEAM sample is compared, **with** a CloudTrail comparison per grant and a drift check of the stacks it touched. By hand until automated: a temporary deviation from D2, which asks for a drift job. No immediate stop yet: deleting the assignment ends new sessions only, so a grant can run up to about 2 h (⚠️ R2.9 #3) | DS | One drill grant reconciled. The revocation Deny SCP follows in phase 2 (2.2) | 7 |
| 1.14 | Risk stop in the deploy job (E7). The policy-finding trigger works from phase 2 | PL, DS | Every prod deploy job runs it | 3 |
| 1.15 | k0s/Firebase deploy credentials moved to secrets of the `production-k0s` environment (OD24); the k0s credential becomes the namespaced, time-limited ServiceAccount token, and the Kubernetes API audit log is on (E11) | PL | No repository secret holds them (E3b); the old admin kubeconfig is revoked; an audit event of a test deploy is found | 1, 5, 7 |
| 1.16 | **Then** remove standing prod write, including Expo roles above Developer for people and the protection of the `production` EAS channel and credentials (OD40) | DS | S1 = 0 | 1 |
| 1.17 | MCP/plugin catalogue v1 (E9): marketplace repository with its rulesets (two approvals, protected release tags, E9b), every plugin pinned by `sha`, local MCP servers as image digests (OD26) | DS | Marketplace live with rulesets; first release tag; first review records | 4 |
| 1.18 | Managed settings, phase-1 subset (E8): `defaultMode` (D1 said "immediately"); `disableBypassPermissionsMode`; `ask` for `aws`, `pulumi`, `serverless` until standing write is gone and after (OD43); `enabledPlugins` for the internal plugin (OD47); the keys that enforce the catalogue (`strictKnownMarketplaces` pinned to a release tag, `extraKnownMarketplaces` with auto-update off (OD26), `blockedMarketplaces`, `disableSideloadFlags`, `allowedMcpServers` + `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`, `disableClaudeAiConnectors`); the OTel exporter with content flags `0`, which is the evidence for D1's auto-mode metric and the plugin events of layer 4; `requiredMinimumVersion`; the `permissions.allow` list of two repo scripts (OD7b; finding 19 of the examples); a `Read(~/.aws/**)` deny rule and `autoMode.classifyAllShell: true` (OD21); deny rules for the `gh` token file, `gh pr review` and `gh api …reviews…` (OD25) | DS | Settings live; monthly export matches git | 2, 8 |
| 1.19 | Deploy-job isolation (OD22): environments `production`, `production-iam` and `production-db` (ADR-0011) with their own OIDC subjects and roles; domain deploy roles bounded to `svc-*` roles with the permissions boundary; install scripts off in deploy and preview jobs, with the allowlist in `tools/ci/`; agent review on PRs touching infrastructure code | PL, DS | E3, E4, E4b live; a test PR's install script does not run in CI | 1, 5 |
| 1.20 | Administrators of the administrators (OD23), phase-1 part: name the management-account group (≥ 2 L3 owners, hardware MFA); remove member-account root credentials through centralized root access (📖 R9.2.5); list where `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` exists | DS | Group recorded in C-03; root credentials absent in prod accounts; inventory done | 1 |
| 1.21 | GitHub identity (OD25): organization requires 2FA (⚠️ check the setting on Team), login register from HR joiners and leavers, outside collaborators without write, classic tokens restricted, fine-grained tokens approved with a maximum lifetime | DS, CO | Register covers every member; 2FA required; token policy set | 1, 3 |
| 1.22 | Evidence store (OD30): evidence bucket with Object Lock (compliance, 6 years) in the log-archive account; nightly export workflow (E13); Actions retention set to 400 days; monthly UI export of the org audit log; Linear template for JIT and data-read requests with its webhook mirror | DS, CO | First night's export in the bucket; first audit-log export; one JIT drill request recorded | 7 |
| 1.23 | Database changes (OD29, ADR-0011): `tools/db/` wrappers for the migration tool in use, the `db-change` ECS task inside the prod VPC with its image, task role (IAM database authentication) and the GraphQL-engine admin secret in Secrets Manager, the CI role that may only start that task (E15), the `sql` deploy job, a `data-owners-<tenant>` team per tenant, with read access to the repository, read by the approval-gate app (not code owners, so no write access) | PL, DS; data owners | One migration and one drill data fix applied through the job | 3, 6 |

**Version floor for item 1.18:** the higher of 2.1.248 (needed by `--restricted`, D3, and above the
2.1.179 plugin-pin fix) and the latest fixed high advisory at rollout. Phase 2 raises it to 2.1.310
(`allowedProviders` needs 2.1.285; monitor blocking under `allowManagedHooksOnly` needs 2.1.310;
📖 settings reference, see the E8 row of [`examples/README.md`](../examples/README.md)).

Done when: a test update without a run raises an alert; an unsigned update is rejected on a test device | PL, DS | 5, 7 |

Done when: no standing GCP prod role for people; spike result recorded; one sealed k0s break-glass certificate | DS, PL | 1, 7 |

| # | Item | Owner | Layer |
|---|---|---|---|

| # | Criterion | Target | Measured from |
|---|---|---|---|

| S2 | No long-lived cloud credential in GitHub secrets | 0 (k0s/Firebase excepted, OD1; Expo, OD40) | Phase 1, after 1.3 |
| S3 | Every prod change approved by a named person other than the author, **before** it is applied | 0 unmatched / 0 late | Phase 2 (2.4); by hand before that |
| S4 | Engineers keep their speed: PR to prod the same working day; approval wait ≤ 1 h in working hours; in the non-prod loop, only the phase-2 steps of OD34 (push and PR at the `!` prompt, a confirmation per cloud CLI call), with prompts per session and PR-opening time measured | as stated | Phase 1 (phase-2 steps from the first phase-2 team) |

where a PR was possible, writes outside the command list, late codify PRs, grants per month; starting

  workflows. In person-days (pd):

  |---|---|---|
  | 1.6 approval-gate app | 10–15 pd | The largest item: GitHub App, hosting in the tooling account, webhooks, reading CODEOWNERS and teams; decision logic exists (E12). No off-the-shelf app with these rules was found (⚠️ not searched exhaustively) |
  | 1.23 database path | 6–10 pd | Depends on Papaya's migration tool (unknown) |
  | 1.13 JIT, 1.14 risk stop | 5–8 pd each | 1.14: adapters checked against real `--json` output first (E7 is ⚠️ on field names). 1.13: the AWS TEAM sample instead of the receiver, if its approval rules meet OD33 (⚠️ not checked) |
  | 1.3, 1.4, 1.19 OIDC, CI deploys, job isolation | 12–18 pd together | Roughly half a day per deploy workflow plus the two environments and roles |
  | 1.22 evidence store, 1.17 catalogue, 1.9 data-read flow | 3–5 pd each | |
  | the other 12 items | 1–4 pd each, 25–35 pd together | Settings, schedules, scans, register, first masking |
  | **Total** | **≈ 75–110 pd** | One person has about 20 working days in 30 calendar days |

  **Minimum headcount:** about 4 people full time for 30 days, which Papaya does not have (GĐ-1).

  removing standing prod write needs, plus the items that may not slip): 1.3, 1.5, 1.6, 1.7, 1.12,

  DevSecOps people plus one platform engineer for about 45 days**, or 1–2 people for about 60 days.
  The other items (1.1, 1.2, 1.4, 1.8–1.11, 1.17, 1.20) move into the first weeks of phase 2 in
  that order; broad read roles stay until 1.9 and 1.10 land. Until 1.20 lands,
  `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` remains a standing admin path from the management account, so
  S1 is reported as "0 except the management account's named group" in that window. Which variant (more people or more
  days) is a decision for Papaya's management.
- **If the approval-gate app is late (degraded mode).** The ruleset ships without the
  `approval-gate` check; GitHub still enforces code-owner review, no self-approval and approval

  data owner) are then checked every night by running E12 over the exported reviews (E13) and

- **Engineering speed (S4).** If S1–S3 are met but S4 is not, engineers will find a way around the
  controls (framing §5, P3b), and S1–S3 will not hold. S4 is measured from phase 1 and reviewed with
  the security metrics, not after them.
- **Exceptions:** a ticket with owner, reason and expiry (layer 8).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Decision logic of the `approval-gate` required check (framework layer 3; gap G19) [design].

The GitHub App that runs this (hosting, key storage, triggers: still open, G19) collects the
input below from GitHub (PR, reviews, CODEOWNERS owners per file, team members), from the
incident register and from the on-call schedule, and posts the result as the `approval-gate`
check, which the ruleset requires (E1). This file is the part that can be written and tested
without a live system.

  exit 0  pass: every rule holds
  exit 1  fail: the check stays red, merge is blocked
  exit 2  input cannot be read: fail closed

Rules:
  R1  An approval counts only if it is an APPROVED review by a human, who is not the author,
      not the last pusher and not the person who triggered an app-opened PR (layer 5; OD5),
      on the PR's head commit or on an earlier commit whose diff against its merge base is the
      same as the head's (OD31). So "Update branch" after another merge to `main` does not cost
      a new approval as long as the PR's own changes are unchanged; a push that changes them
      does. GitHub itself dismisses an approval as stale when the diff changes (📖 GitHub docs,
      "About protected branches"); the gate checks the same thing itself instead of trusting
      it. Reviews carry `commit_id`, `submitted_at`, `user` (📖 R9.1.10).
  R2  Every changed file needs a counted approval from a member of one of its owner teams.
      An approval from the on-call group counts for a file of another team only if the PR
      carries the `incident` label, links an incident that is open now, and the approver is on
      shift now (OD27). Anyone with Triage can apply a label (📖 R9.1.9), so the label alone
      grants nothing.
  R3  A file owned only by the L3 owner team (a process path: workflows, CODEOWNERS, agent
      config, catalogue, SCP and IAM stacks, risk stop, ...) needs counted approvals from TWO different
      L3 owner team members (OD26). The ruleset keeps one approval for the rest of the repository,
      because a path-scoped reviewer rule was not found for GitHub Team (📖 R9.1.15).
  R4  A data fix (`db/<service>/data-fixes/<tenant>/...`, L3-data-write, OD29) needs, besides the
      R2 approval, an approval from a different person who is a member of the team
      `data-owners-<tenant>`. The tenant comes from the path, not from CODEOWNERS, so data owners
      need only read access to the repository, not write (a code owner must have write); a tenant
      without such a team fails the check (fail closed). In an incident the on-call approver stands in for the data owner,
      who reviews it the next working day (layer 6); the check passes with a warning.
  W1  Warning, not a failure: an approval submitted less than MIN_REVIEW_SECONDS after the last
      push, or between 22:00 and 06:00 in the approver's own time zone without an open incident. Warnings go to the
      monthly report (layer 7) as signals of rubber-stamping or of an approval made through a
      compromised login (threat T23). Nothing here can tell a web approval from an API one
      (📖 R9.1.10).

Input JSON:
  {"pr": {"author": "a", "last_pusher": "a", "triggered_by": null, "head_sha": "<sha>",
          "diff_ids": {"<sha>": "<patch id>"}, "last_push_at": "...", "labels": ["incident"], "incident_id": "INC-12",
          "files": {"services/claims/serverless.yml": ["team-claims", "oncall-approvers"]}},
   "reviews": [{"user": "b", "user_type": "User", "state": "APPROVED", "commit_id": "<sha>",
                "submitted_at": "..."}],
   "teams": {"team-claims": ["a", "c"], "oncall-approvers": ["b"], "l3-owners": ["d", "e"]},
   "open_incidents": ["INC-12"], "on_shift": ["b"], "utc_offsets": {"b": 8}}
  `diff_ids` maps commit SHAs of the PR to the patch ID of the PR's changes at that commit:
  `git diff $(git merge-base origin/main <sha>) <sha> | git patch-id --stable` (✅ `git patch-id`
  has `--stable` in git here). `last_pusher` and `last_push_at` are those of the last push that
  changed the patch ID, so a branch update that leaves the PR's changes alone does not make the
  updater the last pusher. A missing ID never matches (fail closed).
  `open_incidents` and `on_shift` are read by the app when the check runs: in phase 1 from the
  incident issues in Linear and the schedule file `oncall/schedule.yaml` (an L3 path); from
  phase 2 from the paging tool (G5).
"""
import datetime
import json
import re
import sys

ONCALL = "oncall-approvers"
L3 = "l3-owners"
DATA_OWNERS = "data-owners-"
DATA_FIX = re.compile(r"^db/[^/]+/data-fixes/([^/]+)/")
MIN_REVIEW_SECONDS = 120  # [design] calibrate from the first months of data
NIGHT_START, NIGHT_END = 22, 6  # local hours, [design]
DEFAULT_UTC_OFFSET = 7  # Vietnam, Thailand; Hong Kong is +8, so offsets come per approver


def _time(s):
    return datetime.datetime.fromisoformat(s.replace("Z", "+00:00"))


def counted_approvals(data):
    """R1: the approvals that count, latest per user."""
    pr = data["pr"]
    excluded = {pr["author"], pr["last_pusher"], pr.get("triggered_by")}
    diff_ids = pr.get("diff_ids") or {}
    head_diff = diff_ids.get(pr["head_sha"])

    def same_changes(commit):
        return commit == pr["head_sha"] or (head_diff is not None and diff_ids.get(commit) == head_diff)

    latest = {}
    for r in sorted(data["reviews"], key=lambda r: r["submitted_at"]):
        latest[r["user"]] = r  # a later review (e.g. changes requested) replaces an earlier one
    return [r for r in latest.values()
            if r["state"] == "APPROVED" and same_changes(r["commit_id"])
            and r.get("user_type", "User") == "User" and r["user"] not in excluded]


def incident_active(data):
    pr = data["pr"]
    return "incident" in pr.get("labels", []) and pr.get("incident_id") in data.get("open_incidents", [])


def decide(data):
    """Return (passed, reasons, warnings)."""
    teams, pr = data["teams"], data["pr"]
    approvals = counted_approvals(data)
    approvers = {r["user"] for r in approvals}
    on_shift = set(data.get("on_shift", []))
    incident = incident_active(data)
    reasons, warnings = [], []

    for path, owners in sorted(pr["files"].items()):
        if owners == [L3]:  # R3: process path
            l3 = approvers & set(teams.get(L3, []))
            if len(l3) < 2:
                reasons.append(f"{path}: process path, needs 2 approvals from {L3} (has {len(l3)})")
            continue
        code_owners = owners
        m = DATA_FIX.match(path)
        data_teams = [DATA_OWNERS + m.group(1)] if m else []
        r2_users, oncall_users = set(), set()
        for user in approvers:  # R2
            domain = any(user in teams.get(t, []) for t in code_owners if t != ONCALL)
            oncall = ONCALL in code_owners and user in teams.get(ONCALL, []) and incident and user in on_shift
            if domain or oncall:
                r2_users.add(user)
            if oncall:
                oncall_users.add(user)
        if not r2_users:
            hint = "" if incident else " (on-call approvals count only with an open incident and on shift)"
            reasons.append(f"{path}: no counted approval from {', '.join(code_owners)}{hint}")
        elif data_teams and data_teams[0] not in teams:  # R4, fail closed
            reasons.append(f"{path}: no data-owner team {data_teams[0]} for this tenant")
        elif data_teams:  # R4
            data_users = {u for u in approvers for t in data_teams if u in teams.get(t, [])}
            if any(d != u for d in data_users for u in r2_users):
                pass
            elif oncall_users:
                warnings.append(f"{path}: data owner stood in for by the on-call approver; review due next working day")
            else:
                reasons.append(f"{path}: data fix needs a second approval from {', '.join(data_teams)}")

    last_push = _time(pr["last_push_at"])
    for r in approvals:  # W1
        t = _time(r["submitted_at"])
        if (t - last_push).total_seconds() < MIN_REVIEW_SECONDS:
            warnings.append(f"{r['user']}: approved {int((t - last_push).total_seconds())} s after the last push")
        offset = data.get("utc_offsets", {}).get(r["user"], DEFAULT_UTC_OFFSET)
        local_hour = (t.hour + offset) % 24
        if (local_hour >= NIGHT_START or local_hour < NIGHT_END) and not incident:
            warnings.append(f"{r['user']}: approved at night without an open incident")
    if not approvals:
        reasons.append("no counted approval")
    return not reasons, reasons, warnings


def main(argv=None):
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    try:
        with open(argv[0]) as f:
            data = json.load(f)
        passed, reasons, warnings = decide(data)
    except Exception as e:  # fail closed
        print(f"approval-gate: cannot read input ({type(e).__name__}: {e}); failing", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    for line in reasons:
        print("FAIL", line)
    for line in warnings:
        print("WARN", line)
    print("approval-gate:", "pass" if passed else "fail")
    return 0 if passed else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def test_oncall_cross_domain_needs_open_incident_and_shift(self):
        # OD27: the label alone grants nothing (anyone with Triage can apply it, R9.1.9).
        self.assertFalse(self.passes(case(reviews=[review("bob")])))
        self.assertFalse(self.passes(case(labels=["incident"], reviews=[review("bob")])))
        self.assertFalse(self.passes(case(labels=["incident"], incident_id="INC-1",
                                          reviews=[review("bob")], on_shift=["bob"])))  # not open
        self.assertFalse(self.passes(case(labels=["incident"], incident_id="INC-1",
                                          open_incidents=["INC-1"], reviews=[review("bob")])))  # off shift
        self.assertTrue(self.passes(case(labels=["incident"], incident_id="INC-1", open_incidents=["INC-1"],
                                         on_shift=["bob"], reviews=[review("bob")])))

    def test_process_path_needs_two_l3_approvals(self):
        files = {WORKFLOW_FILE: ["l3-owners"]}
        self.assertFalse(self.passes(case(files=files, reviews=[review("dan")])))
        self.assertFalse(self.passes(case(files=files, reviews=[review("dan"), review("frank")])))
        self.assertTrue(self.passes(case(files=files, reviews=[review("dan"), review("erin")])))
        # an incident does not lower it: process paths are not co-owned by the on-call group
        self.assertFalse(self.passes(case(files=files, labels=["incident"], incident_id="INC-1",
                                          open_incidents=["INC-1"], on_shift=["dan"],
                                          reviews=[review("dan")])))

"""- **Isolated agent runtime, a phase-2 option (OD58) [design; numbers ⚠️ estimates].** Today the
  agent runs as the engineer: CloudTrail cannot tell them apart (P1a), an injected command can use
  the engineer's SSO tokens (trade-off above), and the sandbox that limits this costs Engineering
  push, PRs and Docker. The option: the agent runs where the engineer's credentials are not, in a
  development box in a non-prod account (or a container under a separate OS user on the laptop):
  - AWS: the box's own role, non-prod accounts plus a metadata-only prod read role that trusts only
    the box's role; CloudTrail shows the agent as its own principal, with the engineer in the role
    session name (how the box sets it ⚠️ to design);
  - GitHub: a short-lived token from a GitHub App per session, allowed to push branches other than
    `main` and open PRs; the ruleset protects `main`, and the approval-gate app counts no approval
    from an app (R1), whatever the token's review permission (⚠️ recalled that opening PRs also
    allows reviews);
  - what it gives: P1a covered for everything done in the box; a stolen token opens only the
    box's roles; Engineering gets back agent push and PRs, Docker inside the box and no prompt per
    non-prod cloud CLI call;
  - cost: about 15–25 pd to build (image, provisioning, token broker, roles) and the compute per
    engineer; laptop sessions and their layer-2 controls stay for those who do not use it.
  It is evaluated with the phase-2 pilot next to OD50's narrow credential (rollout 2.14); Papaya
  decides at the final review whether it replaces phase 3's item 3.3 (§1).
- **Hard limits:** Bash rules are not a boundary (📖 R1.2.6); hooks fail open unless""")
# §1 decisions rows
sub(F,"| Auto mode on laptops | Allowed, measured, with a switch to turn it off | layer 2 |",
"""| Auto mode on laptops | Allowed, measured, with a switch to turn it off | layer 2 |

| The approval-gate app in phase 1, or a lean first version | Build the app: it prevents; the lean version (GitHub's own rules plus a nightly check of the same rules) only detects, and is acceptable only if Compliance accepts it in writing | rollout plan |""")
R="docs/03-rollout-plan.md"
sub(R,"| 2.13 | Prod access on GCP, Firebase and k0s (OD36):",
"""| 2.14 | Isolated agent runtime, evaluated with the pilot of 2.1 (OD58, framework layer 2): a development box with its own AWS role and a per-session GitHub App token; compared with OD50's narrow credential on S4, P1a and cost. Done when: the pilot team used it for two weeks; result and recommendation recorded for the final review (3.5) | DS, PL | 1, 2 |
| 2.13 | Prod access on GCP, Firebase and k0s (OD36):""")

k=t.index("| 2.13 |"); k=t.index("\n",k)+1; t=t[:k]+row+t[k:]
open(R,"w").write(t)
# lean v1 + run cost
sub(R,"""- **If the approval-gate app is late (degraded mode).**""",
"""- **Steady-state run cost (OD57) [design; every number ⚠️ an estimate].** The custom parts need an
  owner after they ship. Per year, in person-days:

  | Component | Run effort | What it is |
  |---|---|---|
  | Approval-gate app (E12) | 15–25 pd | Dependency and GitHub API updates, rule changes, its alerts (answered by the DevSecOps owner in working hours; out of hours it fails closed and the JIT path applies), flagged-approval triage |
  | Risk stop and SQL classifier (E7) | 8–15 pd | Following Pulumi and Serverless output changes, false-positive handling |
  | JIT receiver (E16), Linear mirror, evidence export (E13) | 7–14 pd | Payload changes, failed nights re-run |
  | Reconciliation jobs, settings comparison, monthly report | 15–20 pd | About a day a month plus fixes |
  | Catalogue reviews, managed settings, `data-fix-scan` | 15–30 pd | Depends on request volume (S6) |
  | **Total** | **≈ 60–105 pd a year** | About a third to a half of one DevSecOps person |

  GitHub Enterprise Cloud removes part of the reconciliation and register work (framework layer 3,
  "GitHub plan"). The 24/7 approver and responder rotas are sized by Papaya's engineering
  management (OD51) and are not in this table.
- **Lean first version, a decision for Papaya (OD57).** If the headcount above is not available,
  phase 1 can ship the degraded mode below on purpose instead of the approval-gate app: about

392	
393	**Principle.** The level is set by the damage a change can do. One default path above non-prod: a
394	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
395	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. By default a prod change needs two
396	people: one who makes it and one who approves it; the on-call backup only replaces an unavailable
397	primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how many, with
398	two exceptions: a process path needs two L3 owner team members (OD26), and a PR that touches files of
399	several teams needs an owner of each, except in an incident (OD27). Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level; that adds a
400	second approval by an owner of the same stack, which keeps it to two people (OD8). Confirmed by the owner
401	(OD13): the original author opens the approval PR and the first approver
402	approves it. If the first approver is unavailable, another owner of the stack approves; that makes
403	three people and is recorded as a deviation, counted monthly (OD11). A cross-team PR needs an
404	approval from an owner of each team's files: OD10 allowed one on-call group member to cover them
405	all, but since OD27 that counts only for an incident (layer 3, "Who approves at night"). A real-data read is not a change and has its own rule, L3-data. Incidents use the same
406	path with faster people, not fewer security checks.
407	
408	| Level | What | Examples | Approval | Path |
409	|---|---|---|---|---|
410	| **L0** | Read: non-prod anything; prod metadata | metrics, redacted logs | none | read-only identity |
411	| **L1** | Change in non-prod | deploy a branch to dev; `pulumi preview` on non-prod (needs state-write permission on a DIY S3 backend, 📖 R4.3.3) | author only | non-prod roles or PR pipeline |
412	| **L2** | Routine prod change in code | Lambda timeout/memory, ECS desired count, release | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher | PR → `main` → deploy workflow |
413	| **L3** | High-risk prod change | IAM/SCP; replace/delete of stateful resources; network; `.github/**`, CODEOWNERS, `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/**`, `.claude.json`, `.mcp.json`, `.husky/`, `.gitmodules`, `.ripgreprc`, plugin/MCP catalogue and the rest of the canonical list in layer 5; advisory policy finding | 1 code owner ≠ author, ≠ last pusher. L3 process paths (workflow and agent-config files, catalogue, the SCP stack and the rest of the layer-5 list): **2** members of the L3 owner team (OD13, OD26). The IAM stack and its risk-stop approvals are process paths too (OD32): they create and re-trust the SCP-exempt roles and the permissions boundary, so on-call does not co-own them. JIT cannot change them either, because the SCP lets only the IAM stack's deploy role touch those roles; so in an incident the approval-gate app accepts one L3 owner team member, reached by phone, plus the on-call approver on shift (OD55), and flags it for the monthly report. That is rare by design: the IAM stack holds only those roles and the boundary (OD22); a service's everyday permissions live in its domain stack as `svc-*` roles under the boundary, which on-call can approve in an incident. L3 content inside a domain file (an IAM statement in `serverless.yml`, a stateful delete): the stack's owner, then the risk stop (OD8). In incidents: the on-call approver for deployable paths (OD9); paths that define the process (CODEOWNERS, agent config, catalogue, workflows) wait for the L3 owner team | same path; for IaC changes the risk stop also applies; workflow and agent-config files have no prod diff |
414	| **L3-JIT** | Break-glass | ECS force-redeploy while Actions is down | on-call approver ≠ requester (Options §4b); incidents only, as the author accepted it, for Papaya's sign-off (Options §9 Q2); the on-call approver counts as owner of the service in the request (OD13) | layer 7 |
415	| **L3-data** | Real customer data read | one tenant's failed claim record | an approver ≠ requester and an agreement (GĐ-9); data-owner co-approval [design], beyond GĐ-9; at night, see layer 6 | layer 6 |
416	| **L3-data-write** | Data fix on one tenant's records | retry a stuck payout | a code owner plus a different member of that tenant's data-owner team, checked by the approval-gate app; in an incident the on-call approver stands in and the data owner reviews next working day (OD29) | PR → `sql` deploy job ("Database changes" below) |
417	
418	`CLAUDE.md` and the other agent configuration files are L3, because they define the workflow for
419	the whole team (OD3). With code-owner review on, every PR, L2 included, needs an approval from an
420	owner of the files it touches (📖 R3.2.3, R3.2.7; per-file behaviour ⚠️ not a separate research row).
421	What differs at L3 is **which team** owns the path: L3 paths are owned in CODEOWNERS by a designated
422	L3 owner team, L2 paths by their domain team; and IaC changes at L3 meet the

+370	reviewed PR applied by the pipeline, with the JIT fallback (layer 7) as the only other write path.
+371	The approver reviews the code change that will be applied. By default a prod change needs two

+373	primary (OD2). Higher risk narrows **who** may approve (the owners of that path), not how many, with
+374	two exceptions: a process path needs two L3 owner team members (OD26), and a PR that touches files of
+375	several teams needs an owner of each, except in an incident (OD27). Separately, any prod diff that looks risky stops the deploy, whatever its level; that adds a

+377	(OD13): the original author opens the approval PR and the first approver

+379	three people and is recorded as a deviation, counted monthly (OD11). A cross-team PR needs an

+381	all, but since OD27 that counts only for an incident (layer 3, "Who approves at night"). A real-data read is not a change and has its own rule, L3-data. Incidents use the same

content.text:
Mình đã làm xong cả ba việc bạn giao và commit thành `acc9e2d`, working tree sạch. Lần chạy cuối, `validate.sh` (cả actionlint và zizmor) pass 192 test, zizmor không có finding, link và anchor nội bộ không lỗi.

**Vòng chấm:** người chấm độc lập cho **Hire**, kém hơn một bậc so với vòng trước ("close to strong hire"). Có 11 finding, không cái nào critical. Lý do chính chưa lên strong hire:
- framework vẫn khó đọc sau phần brief và §1;
- tooling tự xây khá nặng cho đội 1–2 người;
- hai chỗ trong rollout và đường xử lý incident mâu thuẫn với chính thiết kế.

Mình đã kiểm lại các claim chính của người chấm trong repo và với `claude --help`; tất cả đều đúng.

**Đã sửa theo lựa chọn của bạn:**
- **Cắt gọn framework (OD52):** framework giảm từ 1.309 xuống 937 dòng. Chi tiết, Gaps và bảng quyết định chuyển nguyên văn sang [07-framework-appendix.md](docs/07-framework-appendix.md); chỗ nào bị cắt thì giữ đoạn tóm tắt kèm link. Sau các mục mới ở dưới, framework lại tăng lên 970 dòng.
- **#1 rollout (OD53):** chuyển deploy từ laptop sang CI (1.4) và một lần diễn tập đo incident lane trở thành prerequisite 9 và 10. Phase 1 lúc này ước khoảng 62–90 person-days (⚠️). Ruleset chỉ bắt các check đã chạy thật; S9–S11 và các dòng register liên quan đã chỉnh cho khớp.
- **#2 IAM stack ban đêm (OD55):** khi có incident đang mở, gate app chấp nhận một L3 owner (gọi điện) cộng với on-call approver đang trực, và đánh dấu để đưa vào báo cáo tháng. SCP giữ nguyên. Đã có rule R3i và test mới trong [gate.py](examples/approval-gate/gate.py); sơ đồ 01 đã render lại.
- **#3 (OD54):** S5 giờ ghi là chỉ đạt trên laptop có MDM; MDM không được thêm vào danh sách quyết định của Papaya.
- **#5 (OD57):** thêm bảng chi phí vận hành, khoảng 60–105 person-days mỗi năm (⚠️ ước tính). Thêm lựa chọn "lean v1" (rule GitHub có sẵn cộng check chạy hằng đêm) vào các quyết định của Papaya. Phần định cỡ rota vẫn giữ như lựa chọn trước của bạn.
- **#6 (OD58):** runtime riêng cho agent (dev box với AWS role riêng và GitHub token cấp theo phiên) được đánh giá cùng pilot phase 2, ở item rollout 2.14.
- **#4 (OD59):** viết lại nguyên tắc layer 3, các dòng L3, on-call và break-glass theo trạng thái hiện tại. Mình bỏ những tham chiếu chỉ cho biết quyết định đến từ đâu, và bỏ meta-text kiểu "17 review rounds".
- **#9 (OD56):** data owner là nhân viên Papaya được chỉ định cho từng insurer, không phải người của insurer.

**Đã sửa thẳng vì sai sự thật hoặc lệch giữa các tài liệu:**
- **Cờ `--restricted` và `--tools`:** `--restricted` bỏ Bash (✅ `claude --help`), nên không còn khuyên dùng cho phiên làm việc hằng ngày. Phiên incident có thêm `Skill` trong `--tools`; việc này cần cho skill chạy hay không thì chưa kiểm (⚠️).
- **Rule `ask` cho cloud CLI:** thêm `sls` và các dạng `npx …`.
- **Câu chữ:** sửa câu về data owner trong brief, chú giải ★ trong threat model, và các tham chiếu cũ còn trỏ về framework.

**Chưa sửa:** tên environment `production-k0s` vẫn chứa cả key của Firebase.

Hiện mới chỉ có vòng chấm trước khi sửa. Toàn bộ loạt OD53–OD59 chưa qua người chấm độc lập nào. Mình có thể chạy thêm một vòng nếu bạn muốn.

Transcript đã nằm trong commit này, nhưng phần hội thoại từ giờ đến cuối session cần copy thêm một lần nữa trước khi kết thúc.
